As the new school year begins, an increasing number of Americans are expressing support for banning students from using mobile phones throughout the entire school day.

With the new school year underway, support for banning phone use in classrooms continues to rise

That's right, it's still July, but summer break is somehow already over. My kids return to school today and tomorrow, marking the second consecutive school year that doesn't start in August.

Every year, Apple rolls out a back-to-school promotion in time for the new school year. Eligible students and educators who purchase select Mac and iPad models before August 27 will receive a gift card of up to $150. Consumers in several states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax reductions during the promotional period.

Although back-to-school discounts are widely popular, the use of smartphones during class is increasingly being discouraged.

A recent survey by the Pew Research Center shows that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones during class. This figure has risen from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025, with only 18% now opposing classroom bans.

The increase in support for a full ban—from the first bell to the last bell, prohibiting phone use for the entire school day—is even more striking. For the first time, Americans are showing more support than opposition for banning phone use throughout the entire school day.

The report also notes that younger adults still show lower levels of support for both classroom and full-day bans, but support has risen across all age groups since 2024. The full report is available here.

What do you think? Should schools restrict iPhone use only during class, implement a full-day ban, or leave the decision to students and parents? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
